title: How to write nested IF statements
task: Chain several IF tests for multi-way decisions — grades, tiers, status labels.

excel.note: Each IF's 'else' slot holds the next IF. On Excel 2019+/Sheets, IFS is the flatter alternative.

explanation: A nested IF puts the next IF where the previous one's "value if false" goes, so the tests run in order until one is true: 85 fails >=90, passes >=80, so it stops at "B". Order matters — arrange tests from most to least restrictive, or an early loose test grabs everything. The last IF's false-slot is your catch-all ("F" here). Beyond ~3-4 levels nesting gets unreadable and error-prone; switch to IFS (=IFS(A2>=90,"A",A2>=80,"B",...,TRUE,"F")) or a lookup table with the closest-match pattern, both easier to maintain.
